topics.topic: Required handling of post-startup symlink replacement at SQLite database or journal paths
questions: After startup, what must happen if the SQLite database or journal path is replaced by a symbolic link, given that SQLite may follow it and no named module or capability detects it before the store call writes?
What must happen when a symbolic link is placed at a SQLite-managed database or journal path after the start-time walk?
If the database file or its journal is replaced by a symbolic link after the startup walk, must the next database operation refuse it, or is this an explicit exception to the symlink invariant?

quotes:
Every file of the directory the store opens itself is opened without following
symbolic links, with Linux's `O_NOFOLLOW` on every open, never first asking
whether the flag exists (A20 rule 3). The database file and its journal are
opened by SQLite, which Python cannot ask to refuse a link: the start's walk
finds no link before the database is opened, and afterwards only the
kernel's user can place one, the directory being private.

A link
found at start stops the start, and one found later makes that store call
fail with nothing written.

`store` holds the connection and the transaction and decides
which record goes into which row; the row statements themselves are executed by
`store_persistence`, its companion, which only `store` calls, over that
connection (below).

A18: the data directory and the one SQLite database — the one connection, opened
at start, and the one transaction of every change — the exclusive start lock,
the content-addressed area of value bytes and file fixtures, the per-run spool,
publishing a file only complete and digest-checked, refusal of symbolic links,
start-time removal of temporary files, and removal of the spools `runs` names.
judgement.why: SQLite-managed paths are expressly excluded from the store's no-follow opening mechanism, while the same texts require every later encountered link to refuse the store call and assign unqualified symbolic-link refusal to `store`.

topics.topic: Required non-Linux startup failure point and sequencing
questions: On a non-Linux host, is startup required to reach and fail the sandbox probe, or may an earlier unconditional `O_NOFOLLOW` use fail, and which module must turn that failure into the stated start-stop outcome?
On a non-Linux host, is behavior outside the contract, or must the process reliably reach the sandbox probe and stop there rather than failing earlier while loading the installation or store?

What must happen when the executable is started on a non-Linux host: must it reach and fail the sandbox probe, may an earlier Linux-specific file-open step fail, or must startup explicitly reject the host before the listed sequence?

quotes:
Here and in rule 2 the path is opened component by component without
following a symbolic link at any of them, each component with Linux's
`O_NOFOLLOW` — the host is Linux (A20 rule 3), so no code asks whether the
flag exists and there is no mode without it —, and the checks and the read
use that one opened file, so the file checked is the file read.

A release runs on Linux and on
no other host (owner, 2026-10-18). The kernel does not test the host: on any
other the sandbox probe of the start sequence (A03) fails and the start
stops, and any Linux on which that probe passes is a host; no version is
named.

`capability:installation.load_installation`: the file is a regular private
file of the kernel's user, one JSON object of the installation's fields; no
service twice among the selected instances or the credentials; every
credential header name an HTTP field-name token and every secret file
reference an absolute path; tokens at least 43 characters and pairwise
distinct; agent names pairwise distinct — in that order, the first failing
one named (A16 rule 1, A17 rule 1, M28).

`capability:store.open_store`: the exclusive lock, private directory, no
symbolic link, removal of temporary files and of value bytes no record
names (A18 rules 1, 2, 4).

`capability:sandbox.probe_sandbox`: `bubblewrap` is present and one probe
execution succeeds (A03 rule 8).
judgement.why: The texts require unconditional Linux-only file-opening operations before the sandbox probe while also stating that every non-Linux start reaches and fails at that later probe.

topics.topic: Owner or capability enforcing the Linux-only release constraint
questions: What owner or capability enforces that the release cannot be installed or launched on a non-Linux host?

topics.topic: Scope of SQLite-managed auxiliary-file exception and fixed journal mode
questions: Which SQLite-created files are covered by this exception: only the main database and rollback journal, or also WAL, shared-memory, temporary and other auxiliary files, and which journal mode is fixed?
